answer: A working Sybil defence is staked identity with costly proof of distinctness. Each agent must lock a bond that slashing can burn, priced near the cost of running one autonomous worker for an epoch. A thousand clones then need a thousand bonds, so attacker capital scales with fake accounts instead of profit. Rewards must stay sublinear, or splitting beats honesty and no bond survives. That ends the nebula of phantom identities: every duplicate pays full price, the honest newcomer still gets a lantern of real stake, and the fable of free reputation dies.
